rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent addressees of ‘Take, read my book’ are the angels; the speaker tells them to read a record that establishes his felicity.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله { هاؤم اقرؤا كتابيه } خطاب للملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final hāʾ in ‘my book’ and the endings of the following verses is hāʾ al-istirāḥa, used at pauses.
rows.anchor: والهاء في { كتابيه } وكذا في أواخر الآيات التالية للوقف وتسمى هاء الاستراحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ẓann means certainty; certainty of meeting the account explains the right-hand record: in worldly life he believed in God and acted righteously.
rows.anchor: الظن بمعنى اليقين، والآية تعليل ما يتحصل من الآية السابقة ومحصل التعليل إنما كان كتابي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ‘pleasing life’ means a life whose possessor is pleased with it; attributing pleasure to the life is a rational metaphor.
rows.anchor: أي يعيش عيشة يرضاها فنسبة الرضا إلى العيشة من المجاز العقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden is elevated in rank and contains delights beyond anything seen, heard, or imagined by a human heart.
rows.anchor: أي هو في جنة عالية قدرا فيها ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر على قلب بشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quṭūf is the plural of qiṭf, fruit gathered from a tree; the fruits are close enough to take as one wishes.
rows.anchor: القطوف جمع قطف بالكسر فالسكون وهو ما يجتنى من الثمر والمعنى أثمارها قريبة منه يتناوله كيف يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed are told to eat and drink whatever is available in Paradise, as a pleasant reward for faith and righteous deeds in their past worldly life.
rows.anchor: أي يقال لهم كلوا واشربوا من جميع ما يؤكل فيها وما يشرب حال كونه هنيئا لكم بما قدمتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The left-hand recipients are the wretched criminals; seeing their painful punishment, they wish they had neither received the record nor learned their account, as previously discussed in al-Isrāʾ.
rows.anchor: وهؤلاء هم الطائفة الثانية وهم الأشقياء المجرمون يؤتون صحيفة أعمالهم بشمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘if only it’ refers to the first death experienced in earthly life; he wishes it had ended him without resurrection and eternal punishment.
rows.anchor: ذكروا أن ضمير { ليتها } للموتة الأولى التي ذاقها الإنسان في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are words of regret: he had treated wealth and power as keys to happiness, protection from harm, and control of what he desired, and had labored for them while turning from God and truth.
rows.anchor: كلمتا تحسر يقولهما حيث يرى خيبة سعيه في الدنيا فإنه كان يحسب أن مفتاح سعادته في الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing that worldly means have collapsed and wealth and children cannot help on this Day, he laments his wealth’s uselessness and his power’s failure; regret now avails nothing.
rows.anchor: فلما شاهد تقطع الأسباب وأنه في يوم لا ينفع فيه مال ولا بنون ذكر عدم نفع ما له وبطلان سلطانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is narrated as an order God gives the angels; ‘it is said to the angels: take him’ is understood by ellipsis.
rows.anchor: حكاية أمره تعالى الملائكة بأخذه وإدخاله النار، والتقدير يقال للملائكة خذوه الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghullūhu is an imperative from ghull: a shackle binding hand, foot, and neck together.
rows.anchor: و { غلوه } أمر من الغل بالفتح وهو السد بالغل الذي يجمع بين اليد والرجل والعنق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are to put him into the tremendous Fire and make him remain bound to it.
rows.anchor: أي أدخلوه النار العظيمة وألزموه إياها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Silsila means chain, dharʿ its length, and a cubit the distance from elbow to fingertips; they place him in a chain seventy cubits long.
rows.anchor: السلسلة القيد، والذرع الطول، والذراع بعد ما بين المرفق ورأس الأصابع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reason for seizing, burning, and chaining him is that he did not believe in God or urge feeding the poor, neglecting them and disregarding their hardship.
rows.anchor: أي إن الأخذ ثم التصلية في الجحيم والسلوك في السلسلة لأجل أنه كان لا يؤمن بالله العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamīm means a close friend; here it is a helpful intercessor, and a disbeliever has no forgiveness or intercession.
rows.anchor: فليس له اليوم ها هنا صديق ينفعه أي شفيع يشفع له إذ لا مغفرة لكافر فلا شفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghislin is runoff from Hell’s inhabitants’ bodies, apparently pus and similar matter; because he did not urge feeding the poor, this is his only food.
rows.anchor: الغسلين الغسالة وكأن المراد به ما يسيل من أبدان أهل النار من قيح ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final phrase describes ghislin: only those burdened with sin eat it.
rows.anchor: وصف لغسلين والخاطئون المتلبسون بالخطيئة والإثم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir reports from Ibn Zayd that the Prophet said four bear the Throne now and eight will bear it on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير عن ابن زيد قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s restriction ‘that day’ indicates that eight applies specifically to Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وفي تقييد الحاملين في الآية بقوله { يومئذ } إشعار بل ظهور في اختصاص العدد بالقيامة

rows.speaker: تفسير القمي
rows.claim: A report in Tafsir al-Qummi names eight bearers: Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus among the earlier people, and Muhammad, Ali, Hasan, and Husayn among the later people.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي وفي حديث آخر قال حمله ثمانية أربعة من الأولين وأربعة من الآخرين فأما الأربعة من الأولين فنوح وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports restrict the eight to Resurrection; some say the Throne means knowledge and its bearers are four from the Prophet’s family and four whom God wills.
rows.anchor: وفي غير واحد من الروايات أن الثمانية مخصوصة بيوم القيامة،

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Ayyashi transmits from Abu Basir, from Imam Abu Abd Allah, that people are called on Judgment Day by the imam of their era; affirmation brings the right-hand record, while denial places one among the left-hand people.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال إنه إذا كان يوم القيامة يدعى كل أناس بإمامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports that apply the right-hand record to Ali or Ali and his Shi'a, and the left-hand record to his enemies, are instances of application (jary), not exegesis.
rows.anchor: وفي عدة من الروايات تطبيق قوله { فأما من أوتي كتابه بيمينه } الخ، على علي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Hakim authenticated a report from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri that a bucket of ghislin poured into the world would make its people stink.
rows.anchor: أخرج الحاكم وصححه عن أبي سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

rows.speaker: صعصعة بن صوحان
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits from Saʿsaʿa ibn Suhan that a Bedouin asked Ali about ‘al-khāṭūn’; Ali corrected him to ‘al-khāṭiʾūn’ and directed Abu al-Aswad to devise grammatical signs because many non-Arabs had entered Islam.
rows.anchor: أخرج البيهقي في شعب الإيمان عن صعصعة بن صوحان قال جاء أعرابي إلى علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Burhan, citing Ibn Babawayh’s al-Duru al-Waqiya, reports from the Prophet that a cubit of the chain placed on the world’s mountains would melt them from its heat.
rows.anchor: في تفسير البرهان عن ابن بابويه في الدروع الواقية في حديث عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The excerpt cites 16:102 for the distinction between a qualified expression and an absolute one; its preceding referent is outside this segment.
rows.anchor: النحل 102، فإن المقيد غير المطلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the questioner demanded punishment in defiance and arrogance, a difficult provocation to bear, the Prophet is ordered to show beautiful patience without despair or complaint; the punishment is near.
rows.anchor: لما كان سؤال السائل للعذاب عن تعنت واستكبار وهو مما يشق تحمله أمر نبيه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بالصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns may refer to the punishment or Judgment Day with its punishment; the author favors the punishment, supported by the following description of the sky.
rows.anchor: ويؤيد الأول قوله فيما بعد { يوم تكون السماء كالمهل } الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Seeing’ figuratively means believing: they deem the punishment impossible, since arrogant rejection of God’s judgment does not fit belief in resurrection, while God knows it will occur and every future event is near.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالرؤية الاعتقاد بنوع من العناية المجازية ورؤيتهم ذلك بعيدا ظنهم أنه بعيد من الإمكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The near punishment grounds patience: enduring hostility is easier when relief is certain to be near; divine knowledge does not fail to match reality.
rows.anchor: وفي الآيتين تعليل أمره صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بالصبر الجميل فإن تحمل الأذى والصبر على المكاره يهون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhl is molten metal such as copper or gold; reported alternatives are oil dregs and tar sediment.
rows.anchor: المهل المذاب من المعدنيات كالنحاس والذهب وغيرهما، وقيل دردي الزيت، وقيل عكر القطران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temporal phrase ‘the day the sky is like molten metal’ is linked to ‘is certain to occur’ in the context.
rows.anchor: والظرف متعلق بقوله " واقع " على ما يفيده السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIhn is wool generally, perhaps fluffed wool as in 101:5; alternatives are red wool or dyed multicolored wool, like mountains of varied hues.
rows.anchor: العهن مطلق الصوف، ولعل المراد المنفوش منه كما في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥamīm is a close relative whose affairs one cares about; the verse shows the Day’s severity, since each person is so occupied with himself that even close kin do not ask after one another.
rows.anchor: الحميم القريب الذي تهتم بأمره وتشفق عليه. إشارة إلى شدة اليوم فالإنسان يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns refer to intimates understood from context; tabṣīr means showing and clarifying, so intimates see one another but do not ask because they are absorbed in themselves.
rows.anchor: الضميران للأحماء المعلوم من السياق والتبصير الإراءة والإيضاح أي يرى ويوضح الأحماء للأحماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may stand independently, answering whether intimates see one another; alternatively it may qualify ḥamīman.
rows.anchor: والجملة مستأنفة في معنى الجواب عن سؤال مقدر كأنه لما قيل لا يسأل حميم حميما

rows.speaker: قول بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say angels show the unbelievers; the author says this and the following readings lack evidence.
rows.anchor: ومن ردي التفسير قول بعضهم إن معنى قوله { يبصرونهم } يبصر الملائكة الكفار

rows.speaker: ما قيل
rows.claim: Another rejected reading is that believers see their unbelieving enemies and gloat over their punishment.
rows.anchor: وما قيل إن المعنى يبصر المؤمنون أعداءهم من الكفار وما هم فيه من العذاب فيشمتون بهم

rows.speaker: ما قيل
rows.claim: A further unsupported reading says misguided followers see their leaders.
rows.anchor: وما قيل إن المعنى يبصر أتباع الضلالة رؤساءهم. وهي جميعا وجوه لا دليل عليها

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ says mawadda can mean wishing or love; the author suggests its wish sense may arise through semantic inclusion (taḍmīn).
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع المودة مشتركة بين التمني وبين المحبة يقال وددت الشيء أي تمنيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author proposes that mawadda may be used for wishing by way of taḍmīn.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون استعماله بمعنى التمني من باب التضمين

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines iftidāʾ as warding off harm by offering a substitute.
rows.anchor: وقال والافتداء افتداء الضرر عن الشيء ببدل منه انتهى

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines faṣīla as a group separated from the tribe through a more specific shared forefather.
rows.anchor: وقال الفصيلة الجماعة المنقطعة عن جملة القبيلة برجوعها إلى أبوة خاصة عن أبوة عامة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others explain faṣīla as his nearest kin, separated from him like close forefathers.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن الفصيلة عشيرته الأقربين الذين فصل عنهم كالآباء الأدنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage escalates beyond intimates not asking after one another: the criminal would ransom himself with increasingly precious relatives, then everyone on earth, if that could save him.
rows.anchor: وسياق هذه الآيات سياق الإضراب والترقي بالنسبة إلى قوله { ولا يسأل حميم حميما } فيفيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminal is anyone implicated in crime, not only a disbeliever; he would ransom himself with his sons, beloved above all, his comforting wife, supportive brother, close kin who shelter him, then all rational beings on earth, to be saved.
rows.anchor: والمعنى { يود } ويتمنى { المجرم } وهو المتلبس بالإجرام أعم من الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His wife had been his comfort and beloved, perhaps placed before his parents.
rows.anchor: { وصاحبته } التي كانت سكنا له وكان يحبها وربما قدمها على أبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brother is a full sibling and supporter.
rows.anchor: { وأخيه } الذي كان شقيقه وناصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here faṣīla is his close clan, which takes him in and embraces him.
rows.anchor: { وفصيلته } من عشيرته الأقربين { التي تؤويه } وتضمه إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘All those on earth’ refers to all rational beings; the hoped-for ransom would deliver him.
rows.anchor: { ومن في الأرض جميعا } من أولي العقل { ثم ينجيه } هذا الافتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes the hope of escape by ransom. The pronoun refers to Hell or the Fire, called Laẓā because it blazes; it burns and tears away extremities and pursues criminals, so no ransom diverts it.
rows.anchor: كلا للردع، وضمير { إنها } لجهنم أو للنار وسميت لظى لكونها تتلظى وتشتعل

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib explains shawa as the extremities, such as hand and foot, citing the expression for hitting a target’s extremities.
rows.anchor: والشوى الأطراف كاليد والرجل يقال رماه فأشواه أي أصاب شواه كذا قال الراغب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nazzāʿa is an intensive form from nazʿ, ‘to pull out’; īʿāʾ of wealth means keeping it in a container.
rows.anchor: إيعاء المال إمساكه في وعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire calls those who turned away from faith and worship, gathered wealth, hoarded it, and did not spend on the asker or deprived; this fits the following exception and mention of prayer and spending.
rows.anchor: أي تطلب من أدبر عن الدعوة الإلهية إلى الإيمان بالله وأعرض عن عبادته تعالى وجمع المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan sūra recounts jinn who heard the Qurʾan and believed its foundational teachings, then records the Prophet’s mission, God’s oneness in lordship, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: تشير السورة إلى قصة نفر من الجن استمعوا القرآن فآمنوا به وأقروا بأصول معارفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is ordered to tell his people the story; God is the revealer, and the object of ‘listened’—the Qurʾan—is omitted because the wording makes it clear.
rows.anchor: أمر للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يقص القصة لقومه، والموحي هو الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: المشهور
rows.claim: The commonly cited range for nafar is a group of three to nine.
rows.anchor: والنفر الجماعة من ثلاثة إلى تسعة على المشهور

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative reported range for nafar is up to forty people.
rows.anchor: وقيل بل إلى أربعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAjab is what prompts wonder by departing from the ordinary; the jinn call the Qurʾan wondrous because its wording and meaning are extraordinary and an unlettered man who could neither read nor write brought it.
rows.anchor: والعجب بفتحتين ما يدعو إلى التعجب منه لخروجه عن العادة الجارية في مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rushd is reaching what is true, the opposite of error; Qurʾanic guidance leads to beliefs and deeds that yield real felicity to those who adopt them.
rows.anchor: والرشد إصابة الواقع وهو خلاف الغي، وهداية القرآن إلى الرشد دعوته إلى عقائد وأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn returned to their people and reported hearing extraordinary recited speech that guides to true knowledge and deeds, bringing genuine felicity.
rows.anchor: فقالوا - لقومهم لما رجعوا إليهم - إنا سمعنا كلاما مقروا خارقا للعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn and humans were created to worship God; the author cites this as evidence of the jinn’s religious obligation.
rows.anchor: وما خلقت الجن والإنس الا ليعبدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn report that they heard a wondrous Qurʾan, were guided to rightness, and believed it; they include believers.
rows.anchor: إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا * يهدي إلى الرشد فآمنا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn say that some are Muslims and others deviate, showing varied religious commitments.
rows.anchor: وأنا منا المسلمون ومنا القاسطون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn also describe themselves as including the righteous and others below them.
rows.anchor: وأنا منا الصالحون ومنا دون ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn who heard a book revealed after Moses affirm its predecessor, follow God’s caller, and say it guides to truth and a straight path.
rows.anchor: قالوا يا قومنا إنا سمعنا كتابا أنزل من بعد موسى مصدقا لما بين يديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾan indicates that Iblis is one of the jinn and has descendants and a clan.
rows.anchor: ويظهر من كلامه تعالى أن إبليس من الجن وأن له ذرية وقبيلا قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis and his clan see humans from where humans cannot see them.
rows.anchor: إنه يراكم هو وقبيله من حيث لا ترونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses derive the Prophet’s mission, divine oneness, and resurrection from the jinn story, then close by indicating the messenger’s protection from error.
rows.anchor: في الآيات تسجيل للنبوة وذكر وحدانيته تعالى والمعاد كالاستنتاج من القصة وتختتم بالإشارة إلى عصمة الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is conjoined to ‘they listened’; God’s ownership of mosques explains the command not to invoke another with Him.
rows.anchor: معطوف على قوله { أنه استمع } الخ، وجملة { أن المساجد لله } في موضع التعليل لقوله { فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here duʿāʾ means worship; God also names worship duʿāʾ in 40:60.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالدعاء العبادة وقد سماها الله دعاء كما في قوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some identify al-masājid as the Kaʿba, the Sacred Mosque, or the Sacred Mosque together with Jerusalem; the author rejects these because a plural does not fit one or two places.
rows.anchor: وقد اختلف في المراد من المساجد فقيل المراد به الكعبة، وقيل المسجد الحرام،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The view that al-masājid means the sanctuary is unsupported and, the author says, a taunt.
rows.anchor: وقيل الحرم، وهو تهكم لا دليل عليه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: One interpretation takes al-masājid as the whole earth, citing the Prophet’s saying that the earth was made a place of prayer and a purifier.
rows.anchor: وقيل الأرض كلها لقوله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That hadith establishes only that worship is permitted anywhere, unlike Jewish and Christian restrictions to synagogues and churches; it does not establish that every place is ordinarily called a mosque.
rows.anchor: وفيه أنه لا يدل على أزيد من جواز العبادة في أي بقعة من بقاع الأرض خلافا لما هو المعروف عن اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes al-masājid as the prayers and interprets the verse as prayer only to God; the author calls it unsupported and a taunt.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به الصلوات فلا يصلى إلا لله، وهو تهكم لا دليل عليه

rows.speaker: الإمام الجواد عليه السلام
rows.claim: Imam al-Jawad says the mosques are the seven bodily members placed on the ground in prostration: forehead, palms, knees, and toes.
rows.anchor: وعن الإمام الجواد عليه السلام أن المراد بالمساجد الأعضاء السبعة التي يسجد عليها في الصلاة وهي الجبهة والكفان والركبتان

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: The body-members interpretation is also transmitted from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Farraʾ, and al-Zajjaj.
rows.anchor: ونقل ذلك أيضا عن سعيد بن جبير والفراء والزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the body-members reading, those prostration sites belong to God by religious designation; duʿāʾ here is prostration as worship’s clearest instance, or prayer because it includes prostration.
rows.anchor: والأنسب على هذا أن يكون المراد بكون مواضع السجود من الإنسان لله اختصاصها به اختصاصا تشريعيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Libad is the plural of libda: accumulated, piled together.
rows.anchor: اللبد بالكسر فالفتح جمع لبدة بالضم فالسكون المجتمعة المتراكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh is the Prophet, as the next verse shows; calling him God’s servant prepares for ‘I invoke my Lord.’
rows.anchor: والمراد بعبد الله النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كما تدل عليه الآية التالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronouns most fittingly refer to polytheists who crowded around the Prophet as he prayed and recited, mocking and raising their voices above his.
rows.anchor: والأنسب لسياق الآيات التالية أن يكون مرجع ضميري الجمع في قوله { كادوا يكونون } المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses threaten those who disparage the Qurʾan by calling it magic and mock truths it contains.
rows.anchor: في الآيات وعيد شديد للطاعنين في القرآن الرامين له بأنه سحر والمستهزئين لبعض ما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naqr is striking, and nāqūr is an instrument struck to sound; striking it is a euphemism for resurrection and the gathering for judgment.
rows.anchor: النقر القرع والناقور ما ينقر فيه للتصويت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘when’ clause is conditional, with ‘that’ and what follows as its apodosis.
rows.anchor: والجملة شرطية جزاؤها قوله { فذلك } الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That’ points to the time of the trumpet blast; yawm idhin may mean the return-to-God day or the time in which the blast occurs, with a time interval containing a shorter interval.
rows.anchor: الإشارة بقوله { فذلك } إلى زمان نقر الناقور ولا يبعد أن يكون المراد بيومئذ يوم إذ يرجعون إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blast’s time on the day of return may be hard for unbelievers, or the blast itself may be hard for them on that day, depending on what yawm idhin modifies.
rows.anchor: والمعنى فزمان نقر الناقور الواقع في يوم رجوع الخلائق إلى الله زمان عسير على الكافرين

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf says idhā is governed by the sense of the apodosis (‘the matter becomes hard’), and yawm idhin can modify ‘a hard day’ because Judgment Day occurs when the trumpet is sounded.
rows.anchor: وقال في الكشاف فإن قلت بم انتصب إذا وكيف صح أن يقع يومئذ ظرفا ليوم عسير؟ قلت انتصب إذا بما دل عليه الجزاء

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf also allows yawm idhin to be an indeclinable nominative substitute for dhalika, yielding ‘the day of the blast is a hard day.’
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون يومئذ مبنيا مرفوع المحل بدلا من ذلك، ويوم عسير خبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Not easy’ emphasizes the day’s hardship: it is hard in every respect, not only from one angle.
rows.anchor: وصف آخر ليوم مؤكد لعسره ويفيد أنه عسير من كل وجه لا من وجه دون وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is a threat; abundant reports say it and the following nineteen verses were revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: كلمة تهديد وقد استفاض النقل أن الآية وما يتلوها إلى تمام عشرين آية نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Best parsing: waḥīdan is a circumstantial accusative of the subject of ‘I created’; God created him alone, then arranged his affairs, so the Prophet should leave him to God.
rows.anchor: وقوله { وحيدا } حال من فاعل { خلقت } ومحصل المعنى دعني ومن خلقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing makes waḥīdan a circumstantial accusative of the object of ‘leave me.’
rows.anchor: ومن المحتمل أن يكون حالا من مفعول { ذرني }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further proposal makes the implied object of ‘I created’ its antecedent: he was created alone, without wealth or sons.
rows.anchor: وقيل حال من مفعول خلقت المحذوف وهو ضمير عائد إلى الموصول، ومحصل المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposal treats waḥīdan as an accusative with an implied ‘I condemn’; the author says the first parsing is best.
rows.anchor: واحتمل أيضا أن يكون { وحيدا } منصوبا بتقدير " أذم " وأحسن الوجوه أولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mamdūd means either abundant and extended wealth or wealth extended through growth.
rows.anchor: أي مبسوطا كثيرا أو ممدودا بمدد النماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuhūdan means present: he sees his sons and draws strength from them; the phrase is coordinated with wealth.
rows.anchor: أي حضورا يشاهدهم ويتأيد بهم، وهو عطف على قوله { مالا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamhīd means preparation and figuratively refers to abundance of wealth and status and well-ordered affairs.
rows.anchor: التمهيد التهيئة ويتجوز به عن بسطة المال والجاه وانتظام الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He hopes for further increase in wealth, sons, and arrangements; kallā rebukes him, while ʿanīd means defiant and boastful of what he has.
rows.anchor: أي ثم يطمع أن أزيد فيما جعلت له من المال والبنين ومهدت له من التمهيد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unnamed report says al-Walid’s wealth and children diminished after this verse until he died.
rows.anchor: قيل، ما زال الوليد بعد نزول هذه الآية في نقصان من ماله وولده حتى هلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Irhāq is forceful enveloping; ṣaʿūd is a steep, difficult mountain path, likening his punishment to being overtaken by an arduous ascent.
rows.anchor: الإرهاق الغشيان بالعنف، والصعود عقبة الجبل التي يشق مصعدها شبه ما سيناله من سوء الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fikr is thinking; taqdīr arranges meanings and qualities mentally by order, precedence, affirmation, and negation to reach a desired conclusion.
rows.anchor: التفكير معروف، والتقدير عن تفكير نظم معان وأوصاف في الذهن بالتقديم والتأخير والوضع والرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Walid sought a claim that would undermine the Qurʾan and satisfy its hostile opponents; after considering poetry, soothsaying, madness, and fables, he chose magic because it divides families and allies.
rows.anchor: وقد كان الرجل يهوى أن يقول في أمر القرآن شيئا يبطل به دعوته ويرضي به قومه المعاندين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘May he be destroyed—how he calculated!’ is a curse like 63:4; repeating it in the next verse emphasizes the curse.
rows.anchor: دعا عليه على ما يعطيه السياق نظير قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence portrays al-Walid after deliberation: he looks to judge, frowns and shows disgust, then turns away and grows arrogant before speaking.
rows.anchor: تمثيل لحاله بعد التكفير والتقدير وهو من ألطف التمثيل وأبلغه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Then he looked’ is the look of someone about to decide a matter on which he was asked to give judgment.
rows.anchor: أي ثم نظر بعد التفكير والتقدير نظرة من يريد أن يقضي في أمر سئل أن ينظر فيه

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines ʿabasa as contracting the face, synonymous with grimacing or frowning and opposed to cheerful expression; busūr is the first appearance of displeasure.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع وعبس يعبس عبوسا إذا قبض وجهه والعبوس والتكليح والتقطيب نظائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away and pride are inner states sequenced after visible facial states because they become evident in his words; fa links his words to those attitudes, not thumma.
rows.anchor: والأمران أعني الإدبار والاستكبار من الأحوال الروحية، وإنما رتبا في التمثيل على النظر والعبوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Qurʾan ‘transmitted magic’ manifests al-Walid’s rejection and pride; he claims it is learned from sorcerers.
rows.anchor: أي أظهر إدباره واستكباره بقوله مفرعا عليه { إن هذا } أي القرآن { إلا سحر يؤثر } أي يروى ويتعلم من السحرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He means the Qurʾan is human speech, not God’s speech as Muhammad claims.
rows.anchor: أي ليس بكلام الله كما يدعيه محمد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
